skill.displayName: Lingxi-MindVault - Auto Memory Extraction for OpenClaw

version.changelog: v1.1.13 fix: 修复 skill.json 格式错误，确保元数据正确

llm.summary: The skill's scripts and instructions largely match the stated purpose (scanning OpenClaw sessions and writing extracted memories to Feishu), but there are metadata inconsistencies (registry claims no required env vars while SKILL.md / skill.json require multiple Feishu credentials) and the skill will read local conversation files and cause their content to be transmitted to Feishu — you should verify scopes, tokens, and deployment isolation before installing.

dimensions.detail: Functionality (scan sessions, extract with openclaw agent, write to Feishu L2/L3/L4, send notifications) matches the skill name and description. However, registry-level Requirements reported 'none' for required env vars while both SKILL.md and skill.json declare required Feishu-related environment variables (FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID). This metadata mismatch is an incoherence that should be clarified.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md plus included scripts explicitly instruct the agent to read OpenClaw sessions.json and .jsonl session files, filter/parse them, call the openclaw agent to produce extraction output, and use openclaw CLI tools to write to Feishu storage and send notifications. All referenced files and commands are within the stated domain (OpenClaw + Feishu). Important security-relevant behavior: the scripts will read full conversation contents and (via the agent/plugins) send them to remote Feishu storage — this is expected for the stated purpose but is sensitive.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No network download/install steps are present; this is an instruction-plus-script package. The skill includes bash/python scripts that are intended to be copied into the user's workspace. No external URLs, archive extraction, or third-party package installs are embedded in the skill files themselves. (The README recommends installing system packages such as inotify-tools/jq via apt, which is standard and expected.)
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The required environment variables declared in SKILL.md/skill.json are Feishu credentials/IDs (FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID) and optional SESSIONS_DIR/NOTIFY_TARGET — these are proportional to the declared purpose of writing to Feishu. The concern: the registry metadata provided with the submission lists no required env vars, which contradicts the skill's own manifests and runtime checks that abort if those env vars are missing. You should confirm which env vars are actually required and inspect the scope/permissions of L2_APP_TOKEN before use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills. It is designed to be run periodically (cron) and will create/append local markers under /root/.openclaw/workspace/memory and use /tmp locks — typical for this kind of utility. It invokes the openclaw agent/CLI to perform remote writes; autonomous invocation of the agent is part of its design but not an unusual privilege in context. Note: default paths are root-owned (/root/.openclaw), so deployment user and file permissions matter.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Key points to consider before installing:

- Metadata mismatch: The registry summary shows no required env vars, but SKILL.md and skill.json require multiple Feishu credentials (FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID). Ask the maintainer to clarify that mismatch before trusting automated install flows.

- Data flow & sensitivity: The scripts read local OpenClaw session files (full conversation contents) and cause those contents to be processed by the openclaw agent and written to your Feishu account. If any conversations contain sensitive PII, secrets, or private data, they will be transmitted and stored in Feishu. Only enable this skill in environments where you accept that data flow.

- Token scope: Verify what L2_APP_TOKEN actually allows (which Feishu app and which API scopes). Grant the minimal permissions necessary. Do not paste tokens or IDs you don't control.

- Deployment isolation: Run initially in a test environment with non-sensitive dummy sessions and test Feishu documents to confirm behavior. Avoid deploying to production/system-wide cron until validated.

- openclaw CLI and agent behavior: The scripts call openclaw agent and openclaw message send. Confirm the local openclaw installation is the expected one and that it doesn't inadvertently forward data elsewhere.

- File locations & privileges: The default paths are under /root/.openclaw — if you run as a different user, adjust SESSIONS_DIR and workspace paths. Ensure proper file permissions so that only authorized accounts can read session files and the .env containing tokens.

- Clean-up & logs: The scripts attempt to clean temporary files, but confirm log locations and rotation (they reference workspace logs). Consider restricting access to logs that might contain extracted content.

If you want to proceed safely: 1) ask the author to fix registry metadata to list required env vars, 2) test with dummy content and least-privilege Feishu tokens, and 3) review/lock down file and cron permissions before enabling periodic runs.
